_about: Which CDISC Library standards each rule package runs against (Plan 2, R6/R9/R10).
Read by RuleCorpusGenerator at PACKAGING time and written into every rules-*.json and into
packages.json. It is DATA on purpose: before Plan 2 the ADaMIG -> SDTMIG companion pairing
lived in engine code (CompanionSdtmDefaults.ADAMIG_TO_SDTMIG), so changing a mapping needed an
engine release. R13: this pairing is a HOUSE CONVENTION - CDISC does not publish it - which is
why it belongs here. The IG -> Model link, which CDISC DOES publish, is deliberately NOT here;
it is read from the product's own _links.model.href (see the plan's Phase 3b guard).
'{version}' expands to the package version in dash form (3.1.2 -> 3-1-2).
Ids are LIBRARY PRODUCT TOKENS, not package short names - the two are different vocabularies
and neither is derivable from the other (measured: the flat form 'sendig-dart-1-1' resolves to
nothing; the slash form 'sendig/dart-1-1' resolves). Always use the slash form.
A standard absent from this map declares nothing, and a run selecting such a package needs an

SENDIG-DART._note: sendig/dart-1-2 is not served by the CDISC Library - /mdr/products lists only dart-1-1, and the pickle has no standards/ key for it. The engine seeds it into the metadata store from the E14 seed supplement (a one-time extract of the printed SENDIG-DART 1.2, ignored once a source serves the key; PLAN-seed-sendig-dart-1-2), so the two dart-1-2 packages resolve on a store seeded by that build. On an older store a run selecting one fails loud and says to re-seed (owner ruling Q1; plan D8). DART 1.2 also exists in the RULES dictionary namespace (sendig-dart/1-2) - CDISC published its rules but not its IG metadata product.

ADaMIG._note: companionByVersion is the table that used to be CompanionSdtmDefaults.ADAMIG_TO_SDTMIG. R10: a version absent here declares NO companion and its standard_domains rules SKIP loudly - there is deliberately no 'newest SDTMIG' fallback any more.

TIG._note: An Integrated Standard: (TIG, 1.0) names no single product, so all four legs are declared primary. R8 permits this - they share one library group ('tig'). No companion entry is needed: the SDTM leg is itself a declared product, which is what retires the isTigAdamRun special case.
